## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The Buddha delivered the teaching while dwelling at the Bamboo Grove (Veḷuvana), framed around the theme of plots to kill him (*vadhāya parisakkana*) [Fausböll 1877].

In the commentary's narrative of the past, set during the reign of King Brahmadatta in Bārāṇasī, the Bodhisatta was born in the Himalayas as the son of a monkey troop leader (*yūthapatiputto*), while Devadatta was born as the hostile troop leader (*yūthapati*) [Fausböll 1877]. After the old leader perishes, the remaining monkeys assemble and consecrate the Bodhisatta as their king [Fausböll 1877]. The Buddha concludes by identifying the troop leader of that past era as Devadatta and the leader's son as himself [Fausböll 1877].
